item.title: Vancouver Whitecaps Manager Comments Expose MLS’ Biggest Problem
item.description: COMMERCE CITY, COLORADO - OCTOBER 24: Vancouver Whitecaps FC head coach Jesper Sørensen looks on during the second half against the Colorado Rapids at Dick's Sporting Goods Park on October 24, 2026 in Commerce City, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty Images Why should fans care about the close of the Major League Soccer regular season if even some club managers admit that results themselves are less important than how a team is playing entering the MLS Cup Playoffs? That question should define the early stages of incoming MLS Commissioner Larry Berg ’s tenure when he takes over for Don Garber after this season, following remarks from one of the league’s top managers this week ahead of what should be one of his side’s biggest matches. What Did Jesper Sorensen Say? Jesper Sorensen’s Vancouver Whitecaps enter Wednesday night’s home tilt against San Diego FC holding a one-point lead on FC Dallas for the top spot and top playoff seed in the Western Conference. The Whitecaps have held the West lead for much of the season, but have seen it dwindle after winning only once in their last six. And ahead of Wednesday’s home clash, Sorensen was asked by a reporter about the importance of maintaining that advantage. “I don’t care about Dallas, I care about us,” Sorensen replied bluntly, but not in anger. “I care about us getting the right feeling of how we play and, yeah. Last year we didn’t talk a lot about first place, and just attacking things. I think now we have been talking about defending first place because we’ve had it for a while, and I don’t think that’s the right way to see it. I don’t go into where we end up. We end up where we end up, I don’t care. What I care about is how we play.” Given the circumstances, Sorensen’s answer made sense. Over his last three games of the season, the Danish manager has to work veteran captain Thomas Muller back into the fold as he returns from a hamstring injury that has kept him out since early October. His team has already been eliminated from Supporters’ Shield contention -- and the continental berth that comes with it -- after Nashville SC clinched that honor last Saturday. And while finishing above Dallas would assure the Whitecaps of home-field advantage in a potential Western Conference final between the two, that’s a lot of ifs. The other postseason benefits are pretty minimal. So yes, for the Vancouver Whitecaps, their best chance of achieving postseason success is to come into the playoffs playing at close to their best, regardless of whether they do so as a No. 1 or No. 2 conference seed. Why Are Sorensen’s Remarks Troubling? For MLS, however, the best chance of capitalizing on the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup is not a competitive model where cases like Vancouvers’ are all too common, adding to the perception that plagues that, relative to other soccer leagues around the globe, the average MLS fixture just doesn’t feel like it matters that much. item.title: The NBA’s DAZN experiment offers warning for the future of streaming RSNs
item.description: Credit: Tomohiro Ohsumi/Bloomberg / Jerome Miron/Imagn Images With the cable-based regional sports network business on its last legs, the open secret among NBA and MLB fans is that leagues will look to launch a streaming equivalent to the RSN. With backing from a deep-pocketed streamer like Prime Video or YouTube, the new service could provide crucial revenue for leagues and teams. But recent events suggest such a strategy might work much better on paper than in practice. Five NBA teams signed exclusive contracts with streaming platform DAZN before this season, placing all local broadcasts on the streamer except a select number of games that would be simulcast on local, over-the-air networks. Yet less than a week into the regular season, following fan outcry , the five DAZN-exclusive teams announced distribution agreements with DirecTV . Because of the initial exclusivity of these deals, DAZN paid substantially higher rights fees for these teams than it did for teams that also kept their local games on linear television this season. The NBA is banking on streamers paying top dollar for its upcoming streaming RSN, which could act as a single hub for watching local NBA games. Streamers are expected to be much more willing to pay for such a service if, like DAZN, the hub can secure exclusivity. But that exclusivity seemed to be the downfall of the DAZN deal. If you wanted to watch every Cavaliers game this season (the team ranked last in Awful Announcing’s NBA broadcast accessibility rankings ), you needed to pay for their local DAZN package, plus Peacock and Prime Video, and then cable or ESPN Unlimited for the ESPN games. There are some ways to reduce this burden. YouTube TV includes games on NBC, Peacock, and ESPN, but you still need to pay for local channels and Prime Video exclusives. There’s no reason to believe that a streaming RSN would look any different. As much as NBA teams like local TV revenue, they rely much more on national TV revenue. That means national TV exclusives, which would remain outside a streaming RSN, would still need consumers to pay for them. Don’t expect the streaming RSN to come cheap either, especially if companies pay up for exclusivity. Similar out-of-market models exist, including MLB.TV on ESPN Unlimited and NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV require significantly more expensive secondary subscriptions. If fans are willing to hold their noses and pay for all these subscriptions, then this isn’t a problem. But the DAZN teams’ move to DirecTV suggests that fans aren’t ready. DAZN would not have given up its valuable exclusivity if fans were flocking to the streaming service in droves. Of course, this could just be a DAZN problem. The streaming service is relatively unknown in the United States. A similar agreement with a more mainstream streaming service, like Prime Video, might have met less friction. item.title: The Final Chapter: 4 Opponents for a Potential Rey Mysterio WWE Retirement Tour
item.description: Photo Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Joseph Sugue, Manager As we inch closer to the end of 2026 with a new year on the horizon, many fans are already speculating about which wrestler might be next to call it a career. One such legend might be closer to the end, as we know: the masked legend, Rey Mysterio. Over the last two years alone, four wrestlers have exited WWE, starting on July 12, 2025, when Goldberg lost to Gunther in his final match at Saturday Night’s Main Event . Next was the conclusion of John Cena’s illustrious career on December 12, 2025, who, fittingly, also lost to Gunther at Saturday Night’s Main Event . To kick off this year, “The Phenomenal” AJ Styles brought his career to a close. He wrapped up his decorated decade with the company at the Royal Rumble in February, losing to none other than Gunther in a retirement stipulation match . Most recently, we witnessed the end of Brock Lesnar’s career following his defeat to Oba Femi in the Night 1 main event of SummerSlam . Despite the loss, he shared a memorable passing-of-the-torch moment with Femi after the match. Fast-forwarding to today, rumors are circulating that Rey Mysterio could be the next star to hang up his boots. According to a number of sources, a retirement tour next year is “quite possible.” Despite the chatter, WWE has yet to confirm any plans, and Mysterio has made no official retirement announcement. Much like Cena, Mysterio has previously stated that he wants to announce his final match well in advance so fans can see him compete one last time. Now, the question many fans may be asking is: why would 2027 be the right time for “The Ultimate Underdog” to call it a career? While a few factors come into play, the most obvious one is his age. Mysterio is set to turn 52 in December. While he has certainly looked incredible throughout his second WWE run – most recently in last week’s Intercontinental Championship Triple Threat match on Raw against Chad Gable and Dragon Lee – he has been relying on stem cell treatments to keep competing. After wrestling for over 30 years, what better time to call it quits than while still being able to perform at a high level? If 2027 does end up being the final time we see Mysterio in the ring, it is essential that WWE give him the proper farewell tour he rightfully deserves. With that in mind, here are four dream opponents he needs to face before calling it a career. CM Punk Kicking off the list is a very familiar rival in CM Punk. Their legendary feud began in late 2009 before peaking in 2010, and while Punk’s character is vastly different today, revisiting this matchup would serve as a great callback to one of Mysterio’s most memorable rivalries. item.description: Pearland running back Royce Swan has 20 rushing touchdowns this season, (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) The penultimate week of the Houston high school football regular season features two marquee matchups between undefeated teams, with Pearland visiting Shadow Creek and Angleton facing Randle in games that will decide district titles. Atascocita has a chance to clinch its 14th consecutive playoff berth against Crosby, while Fort Bend Marshall and Crawford battle for district supremacy and the No. 1 playoff seed. Fulshear and Cypress Springs also meet in a key district clash with serious playoff implications. Here are five Houston-area games to watch this week. Pearland (8-0, 6-0) at Shadow Creek (7-1, 6-0) When/where: 7 p.m. Friday, Freedom Field What to know: No. 12 state-ranked Pearland and No. 9 Shadow Creek have already clinched playoff berths and are already locked into their divisions for the Class 6A playoffs, but the winner here will claim at least a share of the District 19-6A title with a chance to clinch it outright in the final week of the regular season. Pearland has been dominant this year and is now just two wins from securing its second consecutive undefeated regular season under coach B.J. Gotte. The Oilers have won 19 consecutive regular-season games dating back to 2024. The last team to beat them? Shadow Creek. Pearland hasn't let a single opponent come within 20 points this year, and the Oilers have the No. 1 offense in the district at 456.3 yards per game. They are averaging 50.3 points per game, which is on pace to break the program record of 46.7 from 2015, according to Pigskin Prep . Pearland excels at running the ball and has done so to the tune of 303.1 yards per game. Junior Royce Swan has emerged as a star in the Oilers' backfield and is among the Houston area's leading rushers at 1,271 yards with 20 touchdowns. Shadow Creek has a potent offense as well and ranks third in the district at 408.2 yards per game. Passing has been the Sharks' biggest strength, and senior quarterback Tavis Coleman has put together a superb season to lead the way. Coleman, a McNeese State commit, is completing 67.9% of his passes for 1,997 yards and 27 touchdowns without an interception. Sophomore B.J. LaFell, the son of former NFL receiver Brandon LaFell, ranks third in the district in all-purpose yards with 1,015 and has been a difference-maker on both sides of the ball. LaFell has contributed in several facets of the game and has scored a touchdown via rush, reception, pass, interception return and kickoff return. He also handles punting duties for the Sharks. LaFell, who has three interceptions, has helped the Shadow Creek defense become the No. 1 unit in the district at 120.2 yards allowed per game with 14 total takeaways. Senior Caden Watson is one of the Houston-area leaders in sacks with 11. Shadow Creek leads this series 4-2 since 2020, but Pearland earned a 21-14 victory last season. item.title: Milan Keeping Tabs on Manchester United Star Midfielder
item.description: Milan Keeping Tabs on Manchester United Star Midfielder Bruno Fernandes has been dragged down by the ongoing crisis at Manchester United and has had a smaller role than in the past. He also made some pointed remarks after the collapse against Como in the UEFA Champions League, and Michael Carrick publicly contradicted him. According to Calciomercato , the Portuguese star would have to properly force his way out to become an option for other teams, especially Serie A ones. His current contract has a prohibitive €65M release clause. Milan have a clear connection to Bruno Fernandes through Ruben Amorim . He’d be tailor-made for their scheme. However, the playmaker pockets €10.2M per year, which is way more than any of their current players. Both parties would have to make an effort and meet halfway to make the transfer possible. Despite that, the Rossoneri are waiting in the wings to see how the situation unfolds. The renewal talks between the star and the Red Devils are stalling. However, the team has a unilateral option to extend his deal until 2028. A Bosman exit isn’t a looming threat. He was rumored to be close to leaving to head to Saudi Arabia in the summer, but he decided to turn down mammoth proposals to stick around. Our Take on Milan and Bruno Fernandes It’s fair to be ambitious and keep tabs on every potentially enticing opportunity, especially when the transfer market isn’t open, but they’d need a very favorable sequence of events to have a shot. The Rossoneri have splurged on a couple of fees in the summer, but they have been careful with their payroll, as Gonçalo Ramos and Diego Moreira have manageable salaries for top-team standards.

item.title: ‘I would like to be a free agent’: Renato Moicano plans to fight out remainder of deal ahead of UFC Vegas 123 headliner
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - APRIL 04: Renato Moicano of Brazil reacts after a submission victory against Chris Duncan of Scotland in a lightweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on April 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Renato Moicano is ready to bet on himself. The longtime UFC veteran is set to face Tom Nolan in the lightweight main event of UFC Vegas 123, which takes place Saturday at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas. “Money” revealed that he has three fights left on his current deal heading into this weekend’s card, and at this point, he plans on fighting out his deal and testing his worth on the market. “I don’t know [how I feel about that],” Moicano told MMA Fighting. “We have to wait and see. After I fight this [fight], fight the next, and I see how I feel, and how much money I’m making in the UFC. If the money is good, if it’s worth it, nice, let’s go. If not, I’ll have [other] stuff to take care of [me], you know? “I have another business, I have this YouTube, I have the gym, I have other stuff that I’m doing. I’m starting to manage some guys in Brazil, too. I have this MMA show going on Dec. 5. So, who knows? I’m not making any plans.” The 37-year-old recently snapped a two-fight skid — a championship stoppage loss to Islam Makhachev at UFC 311 in January 2025, and a decision loss five months later to Beneil Dariush at UFC 317 — with a second-round submission victory over Chris Duncan in the main event of UFC Vegas 115 in April. Moicano says money talks, certainly, but he seems steadfast on getting his remaining three fights done before making a decision on how he wants to continue his career. “I want to fight this deal out for sure,” Moicano explained. “I want to do the whole thing and then let’s see what happens. I would like to be a free agent, too. … Just to see what it’s like, and in Brazil, I’m getting big, like getting popular. So who knows? Maybe boxing, influencing, something like that, doing all this stuff other than MMA. “So I’m not too worried. I’m not too worried.” Moicano was slated to face Brian Ortega in a rematch on two different occasions this year. First, at UFC 326 in March, and then again at UFC 331 in September. Both times, Ortega was forced to withdraw from the contest. In fact, Moicano reveals the UFC attempted to put the bout together a third time, but is much happier facing a young, hungry fighter like Nolan — a winner of five straight. “I was not expecting [Ortega to withdraw again], so I was a little bit frustrated, but it is what it is, you know? item.description: Since the trip to Provo, Arizona has rattled off five straight wins and finds itself in the middle of the Big 12 title race. However, so are about five other teams including Texas Tech. The tone for the rest of the season will be set on Saturday when Arizona visits Texas Tech. The Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season and offensive coordinator Seth Doege expects them to respond the same way the Wildcats did after the loss to BYU. “I expect Texas Tech to play at their best,” said Doege. “I feel like, you know, you guys asked us questions after losing to BYU. We were pissed off, and we were ready to respond. I expect them to feel the same way.” Doege will have to battle outside distractions as he is making a trip back home. He played at Texas Tech from 2008-12 and is very appreciative of what he learned during his time in Lubbock. Homecoming for Doege Whenever a team goes on the road there are always people guaranteed to be rooting against you, but for Doege it’s a bit different. He’s expecting 30+ family members to be in attendance and while they will always want the best for Doege, they will be rooting for Texas Tech. “My parents still live there, my in-laws live there, we have grandparents there, some of my best friends over at my wedding still live there,” said Doege. “They played there. It’s gonna be fun. Now it’s unique because most of those friends are cheering against me. So that’s unique, but that’ll be fun. So, I’m excited.” With his contingent in attendance on Saturday, he is tasked with blocking out the outside distractions and making sure the X’s and O’s part of the game is ready to go. item.title: Flawed Cowboys defense does enough versus Eagles
item.description: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defense was far from perfect. But they did enough, contributing to a big win against their hated division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 21 points to the Eagles. The first two Philadelphia drives resulted in two touchdowns. After that, the defense would go on to surrender just one more touchdown on the night. Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception. The Eagles converted 23 first downs but were 5-of-12 on third down. Dallas allowed 4.8 yards per carry on 25 rushing attempts, totaling 121 yards on the ground. Individual stat leaders on defense DeMarvion Overshown had one of the best games of his career on his return to the lineup, accounting for six tackles, one interception, two passes defended, and one tackle-for-loss. Shemar James saw plenty of snaps as well, tying Overshown for the team lead in tackles. Quinnen Williams recorded three tackles-for-loss and one sack. This may have been his best performance of the season. Donovan Ezeiruaku also recorded his first full sack of the season. Advanced analytics SumerSports recorded the Cowboys defense finishing with a -.05 EPA/play allowed. This is their best EPA allowed on the season. Furthermore, the Eagles finished with a -.10 EPA per drop back and +0.13 EPA per designed run. The pass defense limited Philadelphia while the Cowboys run defense struggled. The Eagles struggled in success rate, finishing the night at 38.7%. For reference, the league average is typically between 45-50%. Final grade: C This Eagles offense is in absolute shambles at this point in time. They are down one franchise quarterback, two starting receivers, multiple offensive linemen, and too many running backs to count. This needed to be a game where the Dallas defense started fast and never looked back. They eventually got going, but it took too much time against a terrible Philadelphia offensive unit. The Eagles came out and punched the Cowboys defense in the mouth right from the start. The first drive took just four plays in just over two minutes to go 75 yards for a touchdown. item.title: Seven DFAs later, has Josh Walker figured it out?
item.description: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 1: Baltimore Orioles pitcher Josh Walker (61) reacts after pitching in the sixth inning during a game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field on September 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Josh Walker has learned not to take it personally. Well, to be honest, I haven’t actually asked him, but you figure somebody DFA’d seven times in his career—twice by his current team—has developed some thick skin. He’s also developed his game in this, his fourth season, and it was good news for us, because the unsung lefty was an essentially costless addition to the team, and turned out to be one of its best relievers, with a 2.08 ERA in 30 1/3 innings, 29 strikeouts, a 1.19 WHIP, and his first big-league save. Along the way he put up 18 straight scoreless outings, the longest such streak by an Oriole in a decade. You may have heard this story, or one like it, before. Walker was taken in the late rounds of the draft (in 2017, by the Mets, out of the University of New Haven), then saw his career delayed by injury/bad luck. First, a car accident left him needing elbow nerve-transposition surgery. Then the pandemic wiped out the 2020 season. When Walker finally reached the majors, he got hit hard: an 8.10 ERA in fourteen games in 2023 and a 5.11 ERA in ten games in 2024. The Mets DFA’d him, then traded him to Pittsburgh. From there, waivers, waivers, waivers, as Walker made stops with the Pirates, the Blue Jays (a 7.20 ERA in three games in 2025), the Phillies, Baltimore, Atlanta, and Baltimore again. The O’s DFA’d him too, to clear room for Shane Baz, and he cleared waivers in January. Walker entered 2026 with a 6.59 career ERA, little in the way of expectactions, and his season started like this: a May call-up, an option, another call-up, another option, a doubleheader 27th-man cameo, an on-paper move, and then, around August, a quiet turn into the most reliable arm in the Orioles bullpen. item.title: Kyle Larson’s Talladega Win Is Safe. NASCAR’s Yellow-Line Rule Isn’t
item.description: Kyle Larson, 2026 Las Vegas Spring, Cup. Image credit: Nascar9919/Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0) Kyle Larson won Sunday’s YellaWood 500 by going from 11th to first on the last lap of overtime. Within two days, NASCAR was explaining a stripe of paint on its own podcast. The facts first. Larson’s No. 5 Chevrolet passed seven cars in the final quarter-mile at Talladega, beating teammate William Byron by 0.041 seconds. Ricky Stenhouse Jr. and Ross Chastain crossed the line right behind them. It was Larson’s first superspeedway win in 59 tries. He got there in the low lane, after Austin Hill dove low off Turn 2, shucked him into the middle lane and sent him from the lead to 11th. NASCAR reviewed final-lap SMT data and ruled that Larson stayed above the double yellow line. Post-race inspection came back clean, so the win stands. What the line actually punishes The double-yellow rule has existed at Daytona, Talladega and EchoPark since 2001. It was written to stop the apron from becoming a passing lane after a run of wrecks. NASCAR’s crew-chief handout at Talladega in 2020 put it plainly: go below the line to improve your position and you get black-flagged, and force someone else below it and you may get black-flagged too. NASCAR’s Mike Forde spelled out how literal that is in July, after Bubba Wallace was penalized on the last lap at EchoPark. Wallace went below the line beside Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar, said he tried to give the spot back, and ended up second anyway after a push from Ty Gibbs. Forde said on the series’ Hauler Talk podcast that giving a position back doesn’t matter, intent doesn’t matter, and finishing the pass doesn’t matter. A quarter-inch of improvement is enough. He called it a 27-point swing for a driver in the playoff picture. Pack racing at Talladega Superspeedway, where the double yellow line is the only thing separating the draft from the apron. Photo: Carol M. Highsmith / Library of Congress (public domain) A rule this strict needs better proof Put the two rulings side by side. At EchoPark, the standard was geometry, not intent: if a tire was under the line and a position improved, it’s a penalty. At Talladega, the same geometry cleared Larson. That’s consistent on paper. The problem is who can see it. A driver in the middle of a 40-car draft can’t see a painted line under his own left-side tires, and his spotter is watching traffic, not paint. The only people positioned to judge are officials with replay and data, after the fact. My take: a rule with consequences this big and evidence this fine-grained shouldn’t be a black box. NASCAR already walks fans through contested calls on Hauler Talk. The missing piece is showing the work, meaning the actual final-lap positioning data and camera angles, not just the verdict. If the line is going to decide races, the evidence for each call should be public. The loudest case for scrapping the rule hasn’t changed in six years. item.title: Yes, Game 6 of the WNBA Finals is starting early. So, what should we expect from the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream?
item.description: Rhyne Howard attempts to drive on Gabby Williams. | NBAE via Getty Images Much has already been made of the fact that Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals, a potential championship-clinching game if the Golden State Valkyries, up 3-2 on the Atlanta Dream, were to win, will tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET in State Farm Arena. Commissioner Cathy Englebert and WNBA leadership decided to move the game up to half past noon so that the Dream could host 17,000 fans in State Farm Arena, rather than 3,500 in the Dream’s regular-season homecourt of Gateway Center Arena. The NBA’s Atlanta Hawks, State Farm’s primary tenant, have a regular season game later that night, requiring that Game 6 occupy the early afternoon time slot if the game were to remain on Thursday as scheduled. Game 6 of 2026 WNBA Finals to Be Played at State Farm Arena on Thursday, October 29 at 12:30 P.M. ET pic.twitter.com/LBKlWPZZuZ — WNBA Communications (@WNBAComms) October 26, 2026 It’s disgraceful that the Hawks and the NBA couldn’t accommodate the WNBA Finals and move a likely forgettable regular-season game to another date. External of that option, it becomes a battle of preference. While the start time allows for a larger crowd, it will obviously come at the expense of on-air viewership. So, should the league prioritize an in-person atmosphere or a more accessible television viewing experience? How many viewers will be lost by tipping off in the middle of the work and school day? These are questions being answered across the internet, and ultimately the decision has been made. But such debates distract from the main question raised by the early start time: How will it affect the players? Are we going to see half-asleep hoops? In a series that’s already trended ugly, could Game 6 become a particularly brutal watch? Will a sub-optimal start time lead to sub-optimal basketball? Game 5 of the Finals, which the Valkyries won by nine points, featured a battle of insurmountable defenses and insufficient offenses. Both teams settled for a lot of tough 2-pointers, unable to create strong advantages off the dribble or find a rhythm from 3. Quite frankly, it was visually bad hoops. Now, take these elite defenses and wake everyone up at 6 a.m.—if not earlier—to accommodate their routines before an early start time. And perhaps mention the fact that they’re returning from the West Coast, a three-hour time difference. It’s hard to believe we won’t see at least a few players struggle with an earlier start time. These players are professionals, of course, but such a dramatic shift in schedule will impact the bodies of even the most well-trained athletes as they strive for peak performance. Energy output and nervous system calibration are scientifically proven to increase as the day goes on. They’re tied to your internal clock, but don’t change when, on a whim, you wake up at a different time. Your internal clock is difficult to push back. While there’s plenty of historical precedents for Miami to suddenly lose a flukish game, I don’t think it’s controversial to say they’re head and shoulders above the rest of the conference. Other than struggling with a bad Florida State team in a rivalry game, Miami has pretty much rolled their competition. The only other game they were semi-challenged in was against Wake Forest in Winston-Salem back in mid-September. At the time, it looked like a potential warning sign for the Hurricanes; looking back now, it appears to be a solid road win over a top-30 team. Most weeks, one of us here at Tar Heel Blog will write an article on the “X-Factor” of the game. In general, it’s a player/unit/something that could be key in determining the outcome of the matchup. For UNC, having one X-Factor go their way in itself is unlikely to lead to a Tar Heel win on Saturday. For example, I’m pretty confident that the ‘Canes could lose the turnover battle by 1-2 turnovers and still beat the Heels; their offensive is explosive enough to put up points regardless of the occasional hiccup (and Miami only averages 0.5 turnovers a game anyway). The Hurricanes boast one of the best offenses in the country , ranking among the top ten in the country in points per game, yards per game, and several other statistical categories. Miami’s defense is also solid, although not quite on the same level as their offense. They rank 15th in the country in opponents point per game, and their run defense is arguably the best in the country. While their pass defense has allowed some big numbers, a lot of this is from opponents having to throw a lot to try and keep up with the machine that is the Hurricane offense. While it might not be enough to win the game by itself, UNC needs convert on third downs on offense to give themselves a chance to win. This is actually one of the few weak(ish) spots on Miami’s defense; they are allowing opponents to convert on a touch over 38% of their third downs, which is actually right about average for all FBS college football teams. Did ever enjoy the title fights and general excellence of UFC 333? I hope so, because it’s time to drop expectations back to the floor ! item.title: Today in Motorsport History, October 28: Hamilton Clinched a Fifth Title in Mexico in 2018 as Verstappen Won
item.description: Lewis Hamilton at Silverstone in 2018, the season he clinched his fifth title in Mexico City. Photo: Jen_ross83 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) On October 28, 2018, Lewis Hamilton finished fourth at the 2018 Mexican Grand Prix and became a five-time Formula 1 world champion with two races still to run. Max Verstappen won the race for Red Bull, Sebastian Vettel finished second for Ferrari, and the title was settled in a way nobody would have drawn up: by a driver who said afterwards he had a “horrible race.” That mix, a champion crowned on a day he did not win and a race winner who never got near the title, is why Mexico City 2018 is worth remembering. It was the point where a long Mercedes–Ferrari fight stopped being a fight, and where Hamilton moved level with Juan Manuel Fangio on five championships. The competitive context The 2018 season had started as a real contest. Vettel led the championship by eight points at the halfway mark, and Ferrari had the quicker car at several circuits. Then it came apart. Vettel crashed out of the lead at Hockenheim, tangled with Hamilton on the opening lap at Monza, and failed to beat Hamilton in Singapore and Japan, both of which Hamilton won. By the time the paddock reached Mexico, Hamilton led Vettel by 70 points with 100 still available. The arithmetic was simple. Hamilton needed seventh place or better if Vettel won. Anything lower, and the title fight would carry on to the United States or beyond. Mexico City was also a track where Mercedes had been vulnerable: at roughly 2,240 metres above sea level, the thin air robs downforce and strains cooling, and Red Bull had won there the year before with Verstappen. What happened on race day Daniel Ricciardo took pole position for Red Bull, with Verstappen alongside in second and Hamilton third. Ricciardo bogged down badly at the start and Verstappen went straight past into the lead. Hamilton had started well but could not keep Verstappen in sight for long, and he was the first of the front-runners to pit, stopping on lap 12 for supersofts after his ultrasofts wore badly. That was the pattern of Hamilton’s afternoon. His Mercedes struggled to get its tyres to work, he fell back, and Vettel passed him for second on lap 39. Räikkönen ran a quiet race to third in the second Ferrari, and Hamilton could not get back past him. Ricciardo, who had recovered to run second, retired late with a hydraulics failure, his eighth retirement of the year, which moved Vettel up to second place. Verstappen won by about 17 seconds. Valtteri Bottas set the fastest lap, but he finished fifth, one lap down. Max Verstappen at the 2018 US Grand Prix in Austin, one week before his Mexico City win. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . France captain and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe is currently going through a rough patch. Just hours after losing the 2026 Ballon d’Or to Harry Kane, Mbappe also lost several of his collaborations and sponsorships with Chinese companies worth a few million . The controversy began after a video went viral in which Mbappé was heard saying that the funniest meme he had seen of himself was one where his face had been photoshopped onto that of a dictator. And the person in question was Mao Zedong. In China, creating satire or jokes about Mao Zedong, who ruled from 1949 until he died in 1976, is considered disrespectful and remains a social taboo. Shortly after the controversy became a worldwide phenomenon and had everyone talking, Mbappe officially apologized , followed by apologies from the La Liga president. With both a vast reputation and considerable financial stakes involved, Real Madrid, Mbappe’s club, has now publicly apologised . “Real Madrid C. F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé. Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid. “The club joins the public apology expressed by Kylian Mbappé, in which the player himself has conveyed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people. Real Madrid reaffirms its commitment to the values of respect, coexistence, and understanding among cultures, and expresses its desire to continue strengthening the bonds of friendship and affection that unite it with China and its citizens,” Real Madrid wrote. The French captain’s statement on Mao Zedong has been taken very seriously in China, with the Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu freezing Mbappe’s account, as well as Dior and Hublot removing their campaigns with Mbappe. item.title: Henry defends himself after Ballon d'Or criticism
item.description: Thierry Henry finished runner-up to Pavel Nedved in the 2003 Ballon d'Or [EPA] Thierry Henry has defended himself after criticism over the way he hosted Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony. The former France and Arsenal forward, who has come under fire for remarks he made towards Barcelona star Lamine Yamal, overall winner Harry Kane and co-host Kate Scott on the night, has addressed what he said was "people getting really excited about nothing". Henry, who was presenting the ceremony alongside CBS Sports colleague Scott, joked with Lamine Yamal about him winning a third successive young player of the year award. He also corrected Scott's pronunciation of Brazil legend Socrates' name and admitted he wanted fellow Frenchman Kylian Mbappe to beat Kane to the top prize. Addressing the Lamine Yamal situation, which received an audible reaction from the audience in attendance, Henry said he wasn't "checking his ego" and emphasised his admiration of the young Spaniard. On the night, he teased Lamine Yamal by saying of his young player award: "It's your third one, right? But is it the one you really wanted to win?" Speaking in a social media video on Wednesday, Henry said: "I'm a big fan of Lamine Yamal. I wasn't checking his ego at all - that you didn't like the joke, I can understand. "But don't do that, he's one of the players I'd pay to watch, I love him." The 49-year-old also responded to criticism over his response to co-host Scott's pronunciation of 'Socrates', claiming she was in on the joke herself. "You didn't like the joke, I understand, but please stop saying I disrespected Kate," Henry said. "I will never do that and you can ask her, she was on the joke with me. She did Soc on purpose, and I said Soc, so please stop inventing stories." Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka won the Socrates Award for his humanitarian and charity work. Henry added Kane was a "worthy winner" of the Ballon d'Or before telling everyone to "relax" after his support of Mbappe's claim to the prize. "I'm French and I was always going to back up and support my fellow countryman," he said. "I said to [Kane], 'You are a worthy winner, you deserve it, you are the example that work ethic is a talent, working hard is a talent'. Well done, Harry Kane - and I call him Sir Harry Kane since the World Cup. "So please, people out there, relax, relax. I love Harry Kane, I love Lamine Yamal and I didn't disrespect Kate. She was on the joke with me." Ballon d'Or in London - the most chaotic ever? item.title: 'We'll try to make them very happy' - Mikel Arteta demands Arsenal bounce back from Carabao Cup shocker and bring joy to fans at Anfield
item.description: Arsenal FC v Everton - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has called on his players to absorb the pain of their shock Carabao Cup exit before turning their focus toward a massive Premier League showdown. The Gunners were stunned by League Two opposition on Wednesday night, leaving the Spaniard searching for answers ahead of a difficult trip to Merseyside. Gunners stunned before massive Anfield trip Arsenal's Carabao Cup ambitions came to a crashing halt on Wednesday evening as they were dumped out of the competition by Fleetwood Town . Despite Viktor Gyokeres finding the net to cancel out an early opener from the League Two minnows, the north London giants were unable to find a winner in regulation time and eventually fell to a 5-3 defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout. There is little time for the Gunners to dwell on the defeat, as a massive Premier League showdown with Liverpool looms on the horizon. Arteta is aware that his team must move past this setback quickly to maintain their momentum at the top of the table. "We need to take it now on the chin. We are out of the competition, we’re very sad for all the people as well here who came to watch the game - I wanted to give them the victory. Now we need to recover, and get ready for Anfield," said Arteta on the club's official website . Repaying the travelling faithful Nearly 1,000 Arsenal supporters made the long journey to support the team, and their vocal backing was not lost on the manager. Despite the poor result, the fans stayed to show their appreciation for the players, and Arteta is determined to repay that loyalty with a big performance in their next outing. This match marked the beginning of a challenging run of three consecutive away fixtures, making a positive response against Liverpool even more vital for the club's season objectives. Addressing the fans' commitment, Arteta issued a rallying cry ahead of the weekend. "They are always with us. That’s unquestionable, after the game they showed their appreciation to the team, and we’ll try to make them very happy against Liverpool," he stated. Arteta refuses to blame committed players The result from Highbury stadium marks one of the most disappointing nights of Arteta’s tenure, leaving the Premier League leaders to reflect on a missed opportunity for silverware. The Spanish manager was quick to acknowledge the achievement of the opposition while expressing his deep disappointment at the final outcome. item.title: Sergio Garcia And European Legends Face Permanent Ryder Cup Ban
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images A wave of European stars has officially departed LIV Golf, sparking hopes they might return to lead the Ryder Cup team. Yet a rigid regulation from 2017 keeps them on the sidelines. This rule blocks legends like Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Graeme McDowell, and possibly Lee Westwood from serving as captains or vice-captains. The ban remains in place even as tensions between the tours thaw. Ben Parsons reported in Today’s Golfer that the DP World Tour is not expected to change this rule soon to accommodate the returning greats. The barrier stems from a specific regulation added to the tour rulebook in January 2017, long before the LIV Golf disruption began. According to Today’s Golfer, the DP World Tour stated: “Players cannot be a European Ryder Cup captain or a vice-captain if they decline membership of the European Tour or fail to fulfil their minimum event obligation in any season.” Most veterans lured by the breakaway league relinquished their membership for at least one season after joining. A sports arbitration panel in 2023 upheld fines and bans levied against those who competed in conflicting events. Current captain Luke Donald cannot pick from this pool of returning players as he weighs his assistants for the upcoming match at Adare Manor. Leadership roles fall to Edoardo Molinari, Francesco Molinari, and Padraig Harrington so far. Although Poulter and McDowell recently stepped away from LIV 2.0, they were once considered potential skippers prior to joining the Saudi-backed league. The Rule That Won’t Budge The path to leadership for these veterans is blocked by a technicality regarding tour membership. While players like Garcia and Poulter have left the Saudi-backed circuit, the damage to their eligibility was done the moment they dropped their European Tour cards. The rule does not distinguish between a temporary leave of absence and a permanent departure. It simply requires active membership and fulfilled event obligations in every season. As noted by Today’s Golfer, the regulation was designed to protect the integrity of the tour’s event schedule, but it now functions as a one-way door for captaincy roles. The DP World Tour has not signaled any willingness to create special concessions. The pool of eligible captains remains limited to those who stayed loyal or never left. Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia have court-approved separations from LIV Golf and are free to go. However, their past actions regarding tour membership still count. Graeme McDowell added his name to the list of those leaving on Monday with a succinct message on social media. The complexity of this situation increases because numerous players based their choices on the fines and bans they received. In 2023, a sports arbitration panel confirmed these penalties, solidifying the rupture between them and the European Tour.
